lines: The {narrator}, walking with you: "{world} was a continent once. A flood older than any honest map drowned it. We are crossing the top of it."
The {narrator}, half to themselves: "The {energy} you breathe out here is the same {energy} the pre-flood engineers stored. Most of it is theirs, leaking back."
The {narrator}: "The Reclaimers tag, recover, return. The Forgotten Order kneels. The Mud Monarchs collect. The Aetherborn watch. Five answers to one buried country."
The {narrator} glances at the horizon. "Buried cities under us. The flood didn't bury them all at once — some sank slowly enough that the people inside knew."
The {narrator}: "{energy_material} holds light. It holds heat. It holds memory, sometimes. The cores you'll find are not always inert."
The {narrator}: "Mud-glass is dust fused under {energy_adj} pressure during the flood. It traps what it traps. Don't break it without a reason."
The {narrator}, quieter: "Tartarian Giants walked here. Their footprints are in the mud-glass under your boots, if you know what to look for."
The {narrator}: "Etheric Undead are not the same as dead. They are people the {energy} kept past the threshold. They remember. That is the cruelty."
The {narrator}: "The Red Tower in the Order's keeping has forty-seven visible rings. It had more, once. Each ring was a doctrine the Order forgot or denied."
The {narrator}: "Drakova is south. Old Drakova is south, and under. The new Drakova lives on top of its grave and rarely admits it."
The {narrator}: "The Mud Seas are not seas. They are dust over the Cradle of Dusk, and the storms there are {energy_adj}, not weather."
The {narrator}: "Reclaimer code: salvage the relic, return the body, leave the place better than you found it. Most of them keep two of three."
The {narrator}: "{energy_material} Sentinels — the architectural ones — patrol the buried passes. Some have been awake for a thousand years. You will know them when they speak."
The {narrator}: "Tartary above and {world} below — same name, different country. We are walking on the one most maps refuse to name."
The {narrator}, half-amused: "The Monarchs say the buried world is theirs by right. The buried world hasn't responded yet."
